newsitem.title: USA: HIGH PLAINS WHEAT - ISOLATED PROTECTION TAKEN.
newsitem.headline: HIGH PLAINS WHEAT - ISOLATED PROTECTION TAKEN.

text.p: A grain merchandising firm was taking isolated two cents per bushel protection on hard red winter wheat in Kansas, a dealer said Tuesday.

The dealer said the protection was being taken after USDA pegged U.S. wheat production at 2.531 billion bushels, above an average analysts' estimate of 2.476 billion and last year's crop of 2.282 billion.
The estimated increase in wheat production triggered some traders to issue lower opening calls for KCBT wheat futures, which was why the Kansas dealer was taking protection on wheat.
Other dealers in the U.S. Plains said they were not taking protection on wheat.
Meanwhile, basis bids for HRW wheat were mostly unchanged, although some dealers raised their bids slightly in an effort to attract sales.
Basis values in cents/bu against KCBT wheat, cash=dollars/bu.
(Note: U=KCBT September. unq- unquoted, na - not applicable)
